1.

This appeal arises out of the award dated 02.03.2019 passed by 6th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Durg (C.G.), in MACT No.3/2017 awarding a compensation of Rs.2,27,507/- with interest @ 9% per annum, in favour of the appellants/claimants for their irreparable loss.

2. The averment in the claim petition, is that on 16.02.2016 at around 10 AM, due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle (Crane) bearing registration No. CG-7-AN9132 by the driver Omprakash/Respondent No.1, the chain tying plate broke, causing the iron plate to fall on the Bhupesh Yadav vs Omprakash Sahu on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75311925/
1 appellant's Bhupesh Yadav left foot, resulting in severe injuries to all five toes.
Thereafter, he was admitted in hospital for treatment.
Due to the injuries sustained, all five toes of his left foot were severely damaged, and the doctors had to amputate them through surgical operation.
As a result, the appellant became permanently disabled and is now incapable of performing driving-related work that he was undergoing training for.

Therefore, the appellant had preferred an application under Section 166 of the M.V. Act before the Claims Tribunal claiming compensation to the tune of Rs.
37,24,620/-.

3. Learned Tribunal, on a close scrutiny of the evidence brought on record awarded total compensation of Rs. 2,27,507/- in favour of the appellant/claimant with interest @ 9% per annum,
from the date of application till its realization in the following manner:-
S.No. Heads Calculation  01 Towards medical expenses Rs. 26,669/-
 02 Towards transportation Rs. 3,000/-
 03 Towards special diet Rs. 3,000/-
 04 Towards attendant Rs. 1,650/-
 05 Towards loss of income Rs. 13,500/-
 06 Towards loss of future income Rs.1,49,688/-
 07 Towards mental and physical Rs. 10,000/-
 agony  08 Towards loss of facilities in future Rs. 20,000/-
 Total 2,27,507/-
4.
Learned counsel for the appellant/claimant submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side and needs to be enhanced suitably.
He further submits that the income of the deceased assessed by the Claims Tribunal is on the lower side.
No compensation for loss of amenities and future treatment has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
The compensation should be enhanced towards mental and physical agony.

Furthermore, the appellant sustained 22%
permanent disability as per the disability certificate (Ex.P-33) certified by Dr. Akhilesh Yadav (AW-3), but no amount for artificial limb has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal, therefore, it is prayed that the amount of compensation may be recomputed and enhanced suitably.
5. None appeared on behalf of respondents No. 1 & 2 (Driver and Owner).
6.

On the other hand, it is submitted on behalf of counsel for Insurance Company/respondent No.3 that the income of the appellant to be Rs.4,500/- per month assessed by the Claims Tribunal is more as there is no documentary evidence available on record to establish the income of the deceased.

He further submits that though Dr. Akhilesh Yadav (AW-3) certified 22% disability of the appellant but,
the said certified has not been issued by the Medical Board and the Claims Tribunal only on the basis of pleadings and evidence assessed the said loss of income of the appellant.

As regards the artificial limb, neither any doctor examined nor any estimate has been produced by the appellant/claimant, therefore, the Claims Tribunal was justified in not given the compensation Bhupesh Yadav vs Omprakash Sahu on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75311925/
2 towards artificial limb.

7. Heard counsel for the parties and perused the documents on record.
8.
Now this Court shall examine as to whether the compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal is just and proper compensation in the given facts and circumstances of the case.

9. Injured Bhupesh Yadav has stated that he was admitted in Dhanvantari Hospital, Nehru Nagar,
Bhilai for 10 days and in Apollo Hospital for 9 days.
Dr. Akhilesh Yadav has stated that he has issued a 22% disability certificate (Exhibit P-33) but the said certificate is not of the Medical Board.

Dr.
Akhilesh Yadav has admitted that the said 22% disability is due to the injury in the left toe of the injured Bhupesh Yadav.
He has also admitted that it is not mentioned in the certificate that the said disability is of the entire body.
He has also stated that he cannot tell how much his earning capacity was affected due to the said injury because it depends on the nature of the appellant's work.
He has also stated that he had not given any advice to the appellant to get a prosthetic limb or any other equipment.
In this situation, when neither any medical advice nor any estimate has been presented regarding the prosthetic limb, then it is not found necessary to give the amount in that item.
As far as the question of underestimation of income by the injured is concerned?

In this context,
considering the plea of loss of amenities, it is noteworthy that the evidence does not show that the appellant's working capacity was affected and his income was lost to the extent of 22% because the disability of 22% is of only one leg and not of the entire body.
The Tribunal has already assessed the disability of 22% and calculated the loss of future income.

In this situation, the argument of the appellant that a separate amount should be given in loss of amenities or for artificial limbs or some calculation should be made by increasing the income of the appellant is not found to be acceptable.

10. Thus, on the basis of evidence available on record, the compensation of Rs. 26,669/- towards medical expenses, Rs. 3,000/- towards transportation expenses, Rs.3,000 towards special diet, Rs.
1650/- towards attendant, Rs.13,500/- towards loss of income, Rs.1,49,688/- towards loss of future income and Rs.20,000/- towards loss of facilities in the future awarded by the Claims Tribunal is just and proper and requires no interference.

As regards the compensation towards mental and physical agony, looking to the fact that the appellant became permanent disabled and is now somehow incapable of performing his work, therefore, Rs.20,000/- is awarded towards mental and physical agony instead of Rs.10,000/- as awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
Further, no amount has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal towards future medical expenses, looking to the injuries sustained by the appellant, Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards future medical expenses.

Thus, the claimant would become entitled for compensation in the following manner:-

04 Towards attendant Rs. 1,650/-

 06 Towards loss of future income Rs.1,49,688/-

2,47,507/-.
After deducting Rs. 2,27,507/- as awarded by the Tribunal, the enhancement would be Rs. 20,000/-.
12. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed.
The claimant shall be entitled to get Rs. 20,000/- in addition to what is already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount will carry interest @ 6% from the date of enhancement of the award till its realization.

The impugned award stands modified to the above extent and rest of the conditions shall remain intact.
13.

The Registry is further directed to communicate the claimant in writing "the enhanced amount"
in this appeal as against the amount awarded by the Tribunal.

The said communication be made in Hindi Deonagri language and the help of paralegal workers may be availed with a co-ordination of Secretary, Legal Aid of the concerned area wherein the claimant resides.
